After six years of unflinching dedication and thousands of hours of volunteer work, Sadguru Pujya Kothari Swami (Pujya Bhaktipriya Swami) performed the consecration ceremony at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, in Chino Hills, California.

Constructed from 35,000 pieces of meticulously hand carved Italian Carrara Marble and Indian Pink Sandstone, the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Chino Hills, houses five pinnacles, two large domes, four balconies, 122 pillars and 129 archways. From the external walls and domes to the internal pillars and ceilings, the Mandir is completely etched with intricate carvings in marble and sandstone. 

The 6,600 hand-carved motifs depict a mosaic of tales of inspiration, devotion and dedication, along with historical figures from Hindu Dharma. Artisans created the carvings in India with great love, skill and patience before the pieces were shipped to Chino Hills. 

The Mandir is situated on a 20-acre site, complete with a 91-foot lotus-shaped reflection pond, a Cultural Centre, gymnasium and classrooms.

As the first earthquake-proof mandir in the world, the upper structure of the complex is protected from earthquake damage by separating it from the base with a series of 40 base-isolator units. 

The Mandir also uses a solar power system to generate electricity and reduce adverse effects on the environment. The Mandir combines the best of traditional stone art and architecture and the best of modern technology.

Nilkanth Varni writes letter to Guru Ramanand Swami

After arriving at the village of Loj on 21 August 1799 after seven years of intense vicharan on foot, 18-year-old Nilkanth Varni yearned for the darshan of Ramanand Swami. 

When Ramanand Swami did not arrive from Kutch, Muktanand Swami told Nilkanth Varni to pen a letter, which he wrote on 15 March 1800, requesting Ramanand Swami to give him darshan soon.

5 May 2013
Ahmedabad to Sarangpur

On that bright sunny morning in Ahmedabad, Bapa, you took us all by surprise! There were no special or specific programmes planned for that day. Yes, it was Sunday, so Sunday sabha in the evening at Shahibaug Mandir. Yes, it was Ekadashi, so a day of fasting. Nothing more.

The sadhus, parshads and sadhaks in Sarangpur were going about their various seva chores allocated to them as it was a Sunday, a day away from studies. No-one had any idea what would unfold later that day.

That morning, back in Ahmedabad, the one who had never insisted on anything for himself in his entire life unexpectedly insisted. 
'I want to go to Sarangpur!'
'OK Bapa, we can go in a couple of days once the arrangements are done'
'No, I want to go to Sarangpur. I want to go today!'

The rest is history.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj departed in the evening from Ahmedabad to reach Sarangpur. It was to be the beginning of a three-year long stay in Sarangpur. After decades of relentless vicharan, it was Swamishri’s inner wish to stay in Sarangpur for the final years of his life.

events.desc:
During the Sarangpur Mandir Shatabdi Mahotsav, Pramukh Swami Maharaj gave a ‘kol’ to take all to Akshardham. This was to be the final time he gave such an ‘Akshardhamno kol’. 

All were witness to his unparalleled ishta-bhakti on this occasion as well. In every moment of his life, he put God forward. Age, circumstances, the scale of his achievements over all these decades, even the condition of his own body could massively change, but nothing could sway him from his ishta-bhakti. That remained unchanging, because that is who he was, at his core. The same ishta-bhakti he had throughout his life, was the same ishta-bhakti he had in the final year of his life, when his hands could barely move, but he'd still always reach out for his beloved Thakorji, because that devotion to God was never something he learnt or cultivated; it was who he was.

For many around the world, this ‘Akshardhamno kol’ is etched in their hearts as a permanent reminder of the everlasting and eternal peace that the Satpurush can grant. Despite the many challenges, hardships, and miseries life can bring, in such moments, the Satpurush can grant us with bliss. Such reassurances fill hearts with joy and security and make so many fearless in the face of death, disease, disappointment and despair.

Last diksha given by Pramukh Swami Maharaj, as part of Sarangpur Mandir Shatabdi Utsav.

After a lifetime of inspiring hundreds of youths on the path of tyagashram and many joyous, divine diksha mahotsavs, this would be the final time that Swamishri gave tyagi diksha.

From 1971 to 2016, Pramukh Swami Maharaj ordained more than 1000 youths as sadhus. To inspire this many individuals from around the world, at the prime of their life, to give up their personal ambitions, to overcome worldly desires, and dedicate their entire lives to serving society, guru and God is nothing short of a miracle. A miracle stemming from the selfless love, purity, deep spirituality, and godliness of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. 

Alongside inspiring such youths, he inspired parents to happily grant permission for their children to become sadhus. Witness the moving story of one such couple whose son took diksha on that very day: https://youtu.be/Y1WjiRIeTA4?t=3190.

On the auspicious day of Jaljhilani Ekadashi on 2 September 2017, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj performed the murti pratishtha ceremony of Shri Ghanshyam Maharaj Abhishek Murti. He also inaugurated the artistically mesmeric Shri Ghanshyam Maharaj Abhishek Mandapam at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Robbinsville, New Jersey.

The Abhishek Mandapam houses the sacred image of Shri Ghanshyam Maharaj, the childhood form of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. At the age of four, Ghanshyam climbed a pipal tree and looked westwards. When friends asked where he was looking, Ghanshyam replied, “Towards the spiritual aspirants in the West.” 

Ghanshyam was later known as Nilkanth Varni throughout his extensive travels across the length and breadth of India for seven years. He eventually settled in the western state of Gujarat and established the Swaminarayan Sampradaya which continues with a spiritual lineage of gurus to guide aspirants on the spiritual path.

The abhishek mandapam was specially designed to depict the incident from Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s childhood and features a murti of Ghanshyam climbing the pipal tree.

Following the vedic pratishtha rituals, Mahant Swami Maharaj offered the first abhishek to Ghanshyam Maharaj with the waters of 108 holy rivers from India.

Mahant Swami Maharaj met with former President Barack Obama in Washington D.C. 

Mahant Swami Maharaj presented President Obama with a garland as part of a traditional Hindu greeting as well as an Amrut Kalash. Mahant Swami Maharaj also gifted President Obama a sanctified mala and a copy of the book Transcendence.

Mahant Swami Maharaj took time to specifically praise President Obama when he learned that President Obama had set aside time, even as President, to have dinner with his family five nights a week.

Mahant Swami Maharaj was also touched by President Obama’s humility, sharing with the President a verse from a John Bunyan poem, “He that is down, need fear no fall. He that is low, no pride. He that is humble ever shall have God to be his guide.”  

As Mahant Swami Maharaj was departing, President Obama respectfully bid him farewell with the greeting: “Jay Swaminarayan.”

2 September 2017
Robbinsville, USA

On the auspicious day of Jal-Jhilani Ekadashi on 2 September 2017, His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj performed the murti pratishtha ceremony of Shri Ghanshyam Maharaj Abhishek Murti. He also inaugurated the artistically mesmeric Shri Ghanshyam Maharaj Abhishek Mandapam at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Robbinsville, New Jersey.

The Abhishek Mandapam houses the sacred image of Shri Ghanshyam Maharaj, the childhood form of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. At the age of four, Ghanshyam climbed a pipal tree and looked westwards. When friends asked where he was looking, Ghanshyam replied, “Towards the spiritual aspirants in the West.” 

Ghanshyam was later known as Nilkanth Varni throughout his extensive travels across the length and breadth of India for seven years. He eventually settled in the western state of Gujarat and established the Swaminarayan Sampradaya which continues with a spiritual lineage of gurus to guide aspirants on the spiritual path.

The abhishek mandapam was specially designed to depict the incident from Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s childhood and features a murti of Ghanshyam climbing the pipal tree.

Following the Vedic pratishtha rituals, Mahant Swami Maharaj offered the first abhishek to Ghanshyam Maharaj with the waters of 108 holy rivers from India.

Atladra, India

Mahant Swami Maharaj receives Guinness World Records certificate recognising the largest simultaneous Hindu text recital. 

The recognition followed a year-long effort in which 15,666 children worldwide aged between three and 13 years completed the full Sanskrit mukhpath with recitation of the Satsang Diksha, a scripture composed by Mahant Swami Maharaj comprising 315 shlokas that offer guidance for spiritual, moral, social and practical living.

Guinness World Records officials confirmed that 12,723 children were physically present at the venue and were formally counted for the record.

The certificate was officially presented to Mahant Swami Maharaj at the Janma Jayanti Celebrations on 2 February 2025.

The North America vicharan included the Shilanyas Mahotsav for Swaminarayan Akshardham in Robbinsville, in which the ceremony was conducted in Mumbai by Pramukh Swami Maharaj and simultaneously in Robbinsville by Pujya Mahant Swami and Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami on 6 October 2011.

Pujya Mahant Swami arrived in London to give labh for 14 days in the UK.

Interview with press reporter, David Mertns.

At Thakorbhai's home in Thornton Heath in Surrey, Yogiji Maharaj blesses Thakorbhai in abundance for offering his son to be initiated as a sadhu by Yogiji Maharaj.
--------------
Yogiji Maharaj's love drew many yuvaks, inspiring some to renounce worldly life and become sadhus. One such youth was Kamleshbhai, son of Thakorbhai. 

When the family of Thakorbhai readily gave permission for their middle son to become a sadhu and offered him to Yogiji Maharaj during his stay at their house on 12 June 1970, Yogiji Maharaj remarked, â€œBy offering Kamleshbhai to us, it is greater than giving us one million pounds.â€

Kamleshbhai was subsequently initiated by Yogiji Maharaj as a parshad, named Ghanshyam Bhagat, on 14 October 1970 in Gondal on the auspicious day of Sharad Poonam. A short while later, on the auspicious day of Vasant Panchmi on 31 January 1971 in Gondal, Pramukh Swami Maharaj initiated him as Aksharvihari Swami.

Aksharvihari Swami recalls: "When I had the privilege to see Yogiji Maharaj up close, I was struck by his ever-blissful smiling face, innocent deep eyes, saintliness, and simple, tender behaviour. I was initiated as a parshad by Yogiji Maharaj. Despite us being young, careless, and unreliable, Yogi Bapa was always compassionate and gentle â€” with a heart even bigger than an affectionate mother.â€

We visited Ishwarbhai Master's house in Wembley. Swamishri and the sadhus were to eat in a small kitchen, while around 70â€“80 devotees had a buffet dinner outside. When Swamishri entered the kitchen, he saw a few youths peeking through the window, calling, â€œBapa! Prasad!â€

Swamishri signaled Bhaktikishore Swami to serve sweets in the form of pistapak. As Swamishri looked around to find a way to pass the prasad, Bhaktikishore Swami tried to open the window but couldnâ€™t. Swamishri spotted a small opening at the top, tiptoed, and began passing prasad through it.

Soon, more devotees gathered. The sadhus placed wooden stands to support Swamishri. When the pistapak ran out, Swamishri asked for rotlas, broke them into quarters, and continued serving until everyone received prasad.

London, UK

Pramukh Swami Maharaj received two Guinness World Records at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London. 

1. For building the largest traditional Hindu mandir outside of India. 

2. For performing 355 mandir consecration ceremonies (between April 1971 and May 2000).

This was updated in 2007 when Swamishri was awarded the certificate for creating and consecrating a world-record 713 mandirs.

Until his passing in 2016, over a period of 45 years, Pramukh Swami Maharaj built 2 Akshardham mahamandirs, 37 traditional stone shikharbaddha mandirs and 1,192 hari mandirs (a grand total of 1,231 Hindu mandirs) as well as inspiring thousands of families to install ghar mandirs in their homes.

Murti Pratishtha in Ashton-under-Lyne

On Saturday 16 July, almost six years after the Satsang Mandal in Manchester had begun with a handful of devotees, His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj opened a small mandir in Ashton-under-Lyne. The murtis that Yogiji Maharaj had originally installed in Islington in 1970 were re-installed at small premises in Cowhill Lane following the yagna ceremony at The Indian Association hall [The murtis were subsequently moved to larger premises after the property in Russell Street was acquired in 1980].

31 January 1971 

Following Yogiji Maharaj's sad passing on 23 January 1971, he was succeeded by Pramukh Swami Maharaj.

Following in the footsteps of his guru, Swamishri conducted his first diksha ceremony on 31 January 1971 on the auspicious day of Vasant Panchmi in Gondal.

Many parshads received bhagwati diksha in Gondal. The group of initiates included those who had accompanied Yogiji Maharaj from Africa and England, including Kamleshbhai of London, who had earlier received parshadi diksha from Yogiji Maharaj on 14 October 1970.

He became the first youth from London to be initiated as a Swaminarayan sadhu; he was renamed Sadhu Aksharviharidas.

This remarkable painting, created in 1860, is now 165 years old and stands as one of the earliest known visual representations of Gunatitanand Swami Maharaj. At the time, he was around 75 years old, radiating divine serenity and spiritual strength â€”qualities beautifully captured in this historic artwork. 

What makes this painting even more extraordinary is that it is currently the only known and most accurate depiction of Gunatitanand Swami Maharaj. It not only preserves his physical appearance, but also serves as a timeless tribute to his profound wisdom, selfless service, and eternal presence as Akshar, the divine abode of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. 

This sacred image continues to inspire generations of devotees, offering a rare and invaluable glimpse into the divine past.
